meta.scope: Japan batch 6 — Civilian nuclear-power cluster. Covers Strategic Energy Plan nuclear targets, Nuclear Regulation Authority reactor status, JAIF operating performance statistics, electricity generation mix (nuclear share), Fukushima Daiichi decommissioning / Reconstruction Agency nuclear thread, and related spent-fuel / waste indicators. Completes the energy–disaster–security nexus that was only partially covered by earlier disaster and industrial nodes. Definition locked. Note: Japan has no nuclear weapons; this batch is exclusively civilian power and post-Fukushima regulation/recovery.
meta.strategy_note: Addresses the explicit gap identified for nuclear power plants and the post-2011 regulatory/restart regime. Links tightly to the existing Reconstruction Agency / White Paper on Disaster Management cluster and to energy-balance / industrial-production series.

candidates.title: Seventh Strategic Energy Plan (第7次エネルギー基本計画) — February 2025 Cabinet Decision
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) / Agency for Natural Resources and Energy; Cabinet Decision
candidates.description: Mid- to long-term energy policy framework adopted by Cabinet Decision in February 2025. Sets the indicative power-generation mix for FY2040, including approximately 20 % nuclear power (alongside 40–50 % renewables and 30–40 % thermal with decarbonisation measures). Explicitly takes the lessons of the Great East Japan Earthquake and Fukushima Daiichi accident as the starting point, prioritising safety (S+3E: Safety, Energy Security, Economic Efficiency, Environment).
referenced_by: METI Energy White Papers and General Energy Statistics
Electricity generation mix and nuclear utilisation reports
GX2040 Vision and climate/net-zero strategy documents
NRA and utility restart planning that reference the Plan’s nuclear target
International assessments (IEA, IAEA Country Nuclear Power Profiles)
candidates.notes: Prime static + recurring-citation policy node for Japan’s nuclear trajectory. The ~20 % nuclear share by FY2040 is the official benchmark against which restart progress, capacity utilisation and investment decisions are measured. Continuously cited in energy-balance, CO₂ and industrial-policy analysis. Complements the disaster-management cluster by embedding the post-Fukushima safety-first principle into long-term energy strategy.

candidates.title: Nuclear Regulation Authority — Present States of Operation / Reactor Status
candidates.description: Official, continuously updated status of every commercial nuclear power reactor in Japan (in operation, suspended, under construction, under decommissioning). Published on the NRA website and forms the authoritative regulatory baseline for restart decisions under the post-Fukushima New Regulatory Requirements.
candidates.notes: Core regulatory data product. As of mid-2026 examples show roughly 10 units in operation, larger numbers suspended or in decommissioning, and a small number under construction. Direct input into JAIF compilations, METI energy statistics, and public/local-consent processes that govern restarts. Essential edge source for any nuclear-generation or capacity series.

candidates.title: Japan Atomic Industrial Forum (JAIF) — Current Status of Nuclear Power Plants in Japan & Monthly Operating Performance
candidates.description: Industry-standard monthly compilation of reactor-by-reactor status (operable, operating, outage, decommissioning), capacity, utilisation rates, and generation performance. Widely used as the practical reference for the number of restarted units and overall fleet performance since the 2011 accident.
candidates.notes: Complements the official NRA status list with utilisation and generation metrics. Frequently cited in media, market analysis and policy discussion of the nuclear restart pace. Provides the quantitative bridge between regulatory approval and actual electricity output.

candidates.title: Electricity Generation Mix — Nuclear Share (General Energy Statistics / METI)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) — Agency for Natural Resources and Energy
candidates.description: Official statistics on electricity generation by source, including the nuclear contribution in TWh and percentage share. Published within the General Energy Statistics and related energy supply-and-demand reports. Nuclear share recovered to approximately 9 % in recent fiscal years (from near-zero post-2011) and is tracked against the Strategic Energy Plan target.
candidates.notes: The empirical series that measures progress toward the Seventh Strategic Energy Plan’s nuclear target. Direct input into energy-balance tables, CO₂ inventories, industrial energy-cost analysis and national accounts. Links upstream to NRA/JAIF status data and downstream to economic and climate indicators.

candidates.title: Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Decommissioning Progress & Related Statistics
candidates.publisher: Tokyo Electric Power Company Holdings (TEPCO), Nuclear Regulation Authority, Reconstruction Agency, METI
candidates.description: Ongoing official progress reports, technical statistics and monitoring data on the decommissioning of the Fukushima Daiichi plant (Units 1–6), including fuel debris retrieval, contaminated-water management (ALPS treated water), spent-fuel removal, and site remediation. Continues the long-term institutional response that began with the 2011 accident.
candidates.notes: Direct continuation of the Reconstruction Agency and White Paper on Disaster Management cluster. Still produces recurring official data and is cited in energy-policy, environmental and regional-recovery documents. Captures the unique long-horizon technical and institutional legacy of the 2011 nuclear accident.

candidates.title: Spent Nuclear Fuel Storage and Intermediate Storage Capacity / Utilisation
candidates.publisher: Nuclear Regulation Authority, utilities, METI / JAIF compilations
candidates.description: Statistics and status reports on spent-fuel pool inventories, storage utilisation rates (approaching 80–90 % at some sites), and progress on interim storage facilities. Increasingly material to restart decisions and long-term fuel-cycle policy.
candidates.notes: Emerging constraint node. High pool fill rates are cited in media and policy discussion as a practical limit on further restarts or extended operation. Links to both the generation statistics and the decommissioning / waste-management thread.

candidates.title: Nuclear Regulation Authority (NRA) — Institutional Framework and Post-Fukushima Regulatory Regime
candidates.description: Independent nuclear safety regulator created after the 2011 accident. Responsible for the New Regulatory Requirements, conformity reviews, operating licences, and ongoing oversight of all commercial reactors and related facilities. Separated from promotional energy functions previously held within METI.
referenced_by: Reactor status listings and safety-review decisions
Strategic Energy Plan references to NRA-approved restarts
Utility restart applications and local-consent processes
International peer reviews (IAEA, OECD/NEA) of Japan’s post-Fukushima regulatory system
candidates.notes: Institutional node that underpins the entire post-2011 nuclear regime. Every restart is conditional on NRA conformity approval plus local understanding. Continuously cited as the independent safety gatekeeper. Pairs with the Reconstruction Agency as the two distinctive institutional responses to the 2011 triple disaster.

candidates.title: Basic Act on Energy Policy (エネルギー政策基本法) and the Strategic Energy Plan process
candidates.description: Statutory foundation that requires the government to formulate and periodically revise the Strategic Energy Plan. Provides the legal basis for the successive plans (including the Seventh) that set nuclear and overall energy-mix targets.
referenced_by: METI energy white papers and annual energy reports
Diet deliberations on energy and climate policy
candidates.notes: Static legal instrument that is recurringly cited as the authority for the Strategic Energy Plan cycle. Analogous to the Statistics Act or Basic Act on Disaster Management nodes already in the Japan set.
